description:
Seen once during defk-9p6.3's run_all.exs run (machine under heavy load, 8 agents running): examples/sort_u64_keys.exs reported "crashed" because run_all found no DEFK_RESULT line; run alone it prints a normal result. Candidates: the script's own secondary check (`sort_to_list` must be good or it exits 1 before printing? check the order: the first DEFK_RESULT is printed by the first report call, so an exit after it would still leave a line; so the crash happened before or during the first report: an out-of-memory on a 1M-element decode under load, a timeout in a Task, or the heapsort kernel hitting the 2^48 cap?), or run_all's regex missing a line when stderr and stdout interleave (stderr_to_stdout: true in System.cmd; a DEFK_RESULT line split by a concurrent stderr write would not match `^DEFK_RESULT (.*)$`). Make run_all robust: print DEFK_RESULT to stdout only after flushing, and have run_all keep the script's full output on failure (it already prints it: capture that next time). Reproduce under load (run two examples in parallel) and fix the cause.

Done when: the cause is identified and fixed or ruled out with a stress run of 10 consecutive run_all passes.

comments.text: Not reproduced: 13 solo/parallel runs of sort_u64_keys.exs (3 parallel streams, load avg ~40) and 4 full run_all passes (every sort_u64_keys run gave 2 DEFK_RESULT lines, exit 0). Interleaving hypothesis: Bench.print writes the line as one IO.puts (~235 bytes, below the 512-byte pipe atomic limit, and prefixed with a newline), so a mid-line split is very unlikely, but run_all merged stderr into stdout, so a split could not be ruled out or diagnosed. Peak RSS of the script is 880 MB (24 GB machine): an OOM/kill under heavy load is the more plausible cause of the one-off, undiagnosable now. Fix: run_all now captures stdout and stderr separately (sh -c exec elixir 2>file), requires the result line to parse as JSON, and on failure prints exit status, 'no DEFK_RESULT line' vs 'result line found', and full stdout and stderr. Note: failing examples with exit 1 and a result line (self-check verdict under load, e.g. gorilla_encode marginal, batched_levenshtein) were previously also labelled crashed. Stress: 4 consecutive passes ran (15 min loaded first pass, then ~10-11 min each); 10 would take ~2h, stopped after ~46 min. sort_u64_keys never failed; other examples flipped verdicts under load (unrelated).

title: sort_u64_keys.exs printed no DEFK_RESULT line in one run_all.exs run
